sections.h2: What is the Defiance County Recorder responsible for?
sections.html:
Every paper that conveys or burdens land in Defiance County ends up in the recorder's permanent files. The office also takes military discharge papers (DD214s), secures them from public view, and issues free veteran ID cards to honorably discharged veterans without an appointment.

Filing is the office's job. It does not run searches for the public, confirm on your behalf that a mortgage was cancelled, or prepare liens. Anyone may come in and search the public records themselves, and staff will help, and an online document index lets a seller look for a recorded mortgage release before listing.

Landowners can also sign up for a free property fraud alert at propertyfraudalert.com, or by using the hotline number the recorder prints on its page.

sections.h2: What are the Defiance County recording charges?
sections.html:
The office lists $34 for the first two pages of a document and $8 for each page after those. A $5 document preservation fee joined the schedule on January 1, 2025, following Ohio Senate Bill 94, which took effect October 24, 2024 and let counties charge up to that amount per document.

Papers with their own statutory fees skip the extra $5; the recorder names federal tax liens, state job and family services liens, plats, township zoning documents and UCCs. Recording is paid in cash or by check only.

ItemDefiance County charge
Pages one and two together$34
Every page after page two$8
Document preservation fee, from January 1, 2025$5 per document
Marginal notation on a release or assignment$4
Copies made by the public$0.25 per copy
Auditor's conveyance fee$4.00 per thousand
Auditor's transfer fee$0.50 per parcel

Sources: the recorder's page and the auditor's deed transfer page. A page counts for the fee if it has writing on it.

sections.h2: Which approvals does a Defiance County deed need first?
sections.html:
Sellers start at the auditor, because no deed reaches the recorder without the auditor's stamp. The auditor's deed transfer page lays out the sequence.

  1. The county engineer's office checks the legal description, locates the parcel on the tax maps and stamps its approval with a date and signature. The recorder's page gives the engineer's number as 419-782-4751.
  2. For certain splits or subdivisions of less than 20 acres, or with a leftover parcel under 20 acres, the Defiance County Planning Commission must also approve.
  3. A conveyance form travels with the deed. A sale for money pays $4.00 per $1000 at transfer unless an exemption applies, and any deed moving an interest, exempt or not, adds $0.50 for each parcel number.
  4. The auditor confirms that the grantor matches the tax duplicate and that the descriptions agree, then stamps the deed with the fee collected and the parcel count.
  5. The stamped deed goes to the recorder.

A land split adds a tax step. After the engineer approves it, the real estate assessors in the auditor's office work out the tax effect of the split, looking at items such as buildings being transferred and any current agricultural use recoupment charge that may apply to the land. Where a split would leave a parcel under 20 acres, expect the planning commission to be involved too.

Bring these on the day you record:

  • The stamped deed with its fee paid at the auditor.
  • Cash or a check for the recording charge.
  • A self-addressed stamped envelope if you want the original mailed back.

Call the auditor at 419-782-1926 about conveyance requirements before recording, and 419-784-3111 for property value, sales history and tax questions.

sections.h2: What page and margin rules apply to a Defiance County deed?
sections.html:
Check the paper against the recorder's list before you carry it in. A printed or typed name must sit beside each signature, and a "prepared by" line must appear (ORC 317.11). Notary seals must be present, the whole document must be in English or come with a certified translation, and pages must reproduce legibly.

  • Ink is black or blue, type is at least 10 point, and nothing is highlighted.
  • The first page keeps a three-inch blank band at the top; later pages keep one and a half inches.
  • All pages keep one inch clear at the bottom and both sides.
  • Sheets run from 8.5 by 11 up to 8.5 by 14 inches.
  • A self-addressed stamped envelope goes in for the return.

The county engineer must approve some legal descriptions before recording, and releases and assignments need a legal description. Reference earlier recorded documents when a marginal notation is needed. The office lists a turnaround of three days.

sections.h2: How do the Defiance County fees relate to the Ohio statute?
sections.html:
The county's $34 and $8 figures are the sum of two statutory pieces. ORC 317.32 sets a base fee of $17 for the first two pages plus a $17 housing trust fund fee, and $4 plus $4 for each page after that. The recorder's page says the office forwards the housing trust fund share on a quarterly basis and divides the rest between the general fund and the technology fund.

The statute also names smaller items that a seller may meet during a sale. A certified copy costs a base fee of $1 plus a $1 housing trust fund fee per page, a recorder's seal on a certification adds $0.50 plus $0.50, and a marginal reference entered by a separate instrument costs $2 plus $2. Defiance County lists a flat $4 for marginal notations on a release or assignment, so ask the office which figure applies to a mortgage release you plan to record.

Because recording is by mail often, the practical points are short. Send cash or a check, add a self-addressed stamped envelope, and allow the three days the office lists for turnaround. The fee schedule is posted on the recorder's page, and a call to the office confirms the total before you mail anything.

sections.h2: What is Defiance County like for a seller?
sections.html:
Defiance County sits in northwest Ohio along the Indiana line. It covers 414 square miles, of which about 411 are land, and it borders Williams, Henry, Putnam and Paulding counties in Ohio and Allen and DeKalb counties in Indiana. The city of Defiance is the county seat and largest city, named for the old fort that gave the county its name.

The 2020 census counted 38,286 people and 16,539 housing units, with 6.4 percent of units vacant. Of occupied homes, 76.1 percent were owner-occupied and 23.9 percent rented. About 46.4 percent of residents lived in urban areas and 53.6 percent in rural ones, so a seller may hold a town lot or a house on acreage.

Defiance has long been a manufacturing community, anchored for decades by a General Motors foundry that employed more than 5,000 people at its peak.

The median age was 41.4 and 20.0 percent of residents were 65 or older. The count showed 15,482 households, of which 27.8 percent were one-person households. The county takes its name from Fort Defiance, an early army post named by Anthony Wayne, and the Defiance micropolitan area covers the whole county. Sellers who hold long-owned parcels should confirm legal descriptions with the engineer before a deed goes to the auditor, since that office will not transfer a deed without its approval stamp.

faqs.q: What will a Defiance County deed cost to file?
faqs.a: Expect $34 for the first pair of pages, $8 for each page beyond those, and the $5 preservation fee in force since January 1, 2025. Pay with cash or a check.

faqs.q: Does the auditor see a Defiance County deed first?
faqs.a: Yes. The engineer approves the legal description, then the auditor collects its fees and stamps the deed, and only then does the recorder file it.

faqs.q: What rate does the Defiance County auditor charge on a sale?
faqs.a: The recorder's page prints $4.00 per thousand as the conveyance fee and $0.50 per parcel as the transfer fee. An exempt deed skips the first but still carries the second.

faqs.q: Will the recorder's staff correct a flawed deed?
faqs.a: No. The office may not engage in the unauthorized practice of law, which rules out drafting papers or giving legal advice. An attorney or title company should prepare the deed.

faqs.q: Can I look up Defiance County records from home?
faqs.a: Yes, through the online document index in AVA Land Records. A seller can use it to see if a mortgage release was recorded, then visit the office for anything the index lacks.
